subject: Private GPU pool performance alignment with EmberCloud (throughput & scaling)
messages:
From: Julia Wong <julia.wong@embercloud.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial throughput targets + constraints for private pool

Hi Monica / Grace / Rishi,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding call this morning. EmberCloud is evaluating Redwood Private for our inference stack and we need help sizing the private GPU pool and confirming network/design constraints before procurement. High level requirements: 
- Sustained peak: 1,500 requests/sec for text generation (average request = 120 tokens).
- Spike tolerance: 2,500 rps bursts for up to 10 minutes (can be queued).
- P99 generation latency target: <= 1.2s (end-to-end from app to token stream start).
- Cold-start tolerance: up to 2s for rare model reloads, but ideally <500ms after KV warmup.
- Data residency: all inference traffic stays in our VPC; outbound egress must go via our NAT gateways.

Attached a sample load profile and some network traces from last week. Can you sketch an initial sizing and recommend autoscaling behavior, warmup strategies, and expected per-token costs for the baseline config? Also let us know what info you'd need for a formal proposal.

Attachments: ember_load_profile.csv (CSV), network-trace-20271126.pcap (PCAP)

Thanks,
Julia Wong
Director, Platform Engineering | EmberCloud
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Julia Wong <julia.wong@embercloud.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-26T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial throughput targets + constraints for private pool

Julia — thanks, received the traces and profile. Quick clarifying questions before we size:
1) Request mix: are the 1.5k rps primarily short single-turn generations, or do you have a 20% chat/streaming subset that keeps KV cache hot?
2) Model family/size: which model variant do you plan to run in the private pool (open checkpoints / quantized weights)? If unsure, we can provide sizing for two variants (llama-2-70B q4 and a 13B FP16).
3) Failure modes: do you want the pool to auto-fallback to a smaller model under overload, or would you prefer to queue and maintain latency SLOs?

Prelim thought: for 1.5k sustained rps with an average 120-token output, assuming a 13B FP16 model and optimized kernels, we'd target ~6-8 dedicated A10032-equivalent GPUs for steady-state with continuous batching and prefix caching; burst headroom to 12 GPUs with fast spin-up (policy-based warm pool). But that is very rough — I want to confirm the mix and model.

If you’re free, I can run a short sizing call Wednesday to align and follow with a formal capacity proposal (attachment: capacity-proposal-v1.pdf).

—Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@embercloud.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, Julia Wong <julia.wong@embercloud.com>
Date: 2027-11-27T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial throughput targets + constraints for private pool

Monica — quick answers inline (quoted):

> 1) Request mix: are the 1.5k rps primarily short single-turn generations, or do you have a 20% chat/streaming subset that keeps KV cache hot?

Mostly single-turn inference (75% short gens), ~25% multi-turn sessions that depend on KV cache. The multi-turns average ~350 tokens total per session.

> 2) Model family/size: which model variant do you plan to run in the private pool (open checkpoints / quantized weights)?

We plan to run a quantized 13B variant (q4) for latency/cost balance; we may test a 70B quantized variant for a small % of traffic later.

> 3) Failure modes: do you want the pool to auto-fallback to a smaller model under overload, or would you prefer to queue and maintain latency SLOs?

Prefer graceful degradation: fallback to a smaller 7B quantized model for non-critical requests, queue for premium users. Also want region-failover and an SLA window for warmups.

I've attached the detailed load profile (same CSV) and a short note on how we handle premium queues. Also, note our VPC has limited NAT throughput (single appliance peered). Let us know if we should expect egress bottlenecks.

Attachments: ember_load_profile.csv (CSV)

—Carlos Reyes
Senior Engineer, Edge Infrastructure | EmberCloud
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Julia Wong <julia.wong@embercloud.com>, Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@embercloud.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-28T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial throughput targets + constraints for private pool

Thanks Carlos — this is helpful. Attached is our capacity-proposal-v1.pdf with a summary; key points below (executive summary):

- Baseline steady-state (13B q4): 8 A10032-equivalent GPUs
  - Assumptions: continuous batching with 32-batch average, 120-token average, KV cache hit-rate 70% for multi-turns.
- Burst headroom: scale to 12 GPUs within a 3–5 minute warmup window using a warm pool of 4 kept-warm instances (warm pool are pre-loaded model replicas ready to accept traffic).
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to 7B q4 replicas for low-priority traffic; premium routes preserved on baseline GPUs. This reduces SLO breaches during sustained spikes.
- Network recommendations:
  - Ensure NAT gateway throughput >= 3 Gbps for egress to logging/observability endpoints (we measured spikes that could saturate a single appliance).
  - Use dedicated subnet and enforce IPTABLES rules to avoid metadata/service call storms.
  - TLS termination stays in-customer VPC; Redwood agents communicate outbound only over mutual TLS to our control plane (no inbound from Redwood).
- Cost estimate (prelim): ~monthly cost X for baseline 8-GPU private pool + storage and networking. See PDF for line items and per-token guidance.
- Operational runbook highlights:
  - Cache warmup: pre-warm key KV prefixes nightly and before weekday biz hours; maintain 20-minute rolling cache re-warm windows when models are reloaded.
  - Autoscale policy: scale-out at sustained >75% CPU/GPU util for 3 mins; scale-in after stable <50% for 10 mins with min capacity of 6 GPUs to avoid churn.
  - Observability: per-route token-level latency histograms and queue depth alerts at 90% of burst capacity.

Next steps I propose: 1) quick review call to lock down the fallback vs queueing policy (30 mins), 2) sign-off on proposal and procurement SKU list, 3) run a 72-hour pilot with synthetic load to validate warmup times and NAT throughput.

Attachments: capacity-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF), network-trace-20271126.pcap (PCAP)

Let me know availability for the review call.

—Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
